messages:
jonah: quick note — hit a weird correctness case with long-lived streaming cursors + prefix cache eviction during a load test. client resumes and we end up serving tokens from a stale prefix snapshot, not current KV. reproducible in local sim.

maya: ouch. can you paste a short repro or logs?

jonah: yep. repro summary: open streaming convo, KV prefix A is cached, then we evict A (soft eviction), an async rehydrate race fetches new prefix but the old cursor still points at old residency id. output continues using old cache entries until a new seq updates the cursor. logs: 
```
[2026-02-03T14:12:03Z] cursor=cur123 resid=rid42 serving from cache v=7
[2026-02-03T14:12:04Z] eviction soft: prefix=A resid=rid42 -> mark soft-evict
[2026-02-03T14:12:04Z] rehydrate start -> fetch new resid=rid84 v=8
[2026-02-03T14:12:04Z] cursor=cur123 resumed -> still bound to resid=rid42 v=7
```

jonah: so client sees a gap / malformed continuity.

lee: is this specific to soft evict (grace window) or also hard evict?

jonah: mostly soft because we keep old residency in memory for a bit, which confuses cursors that were never pinned to the new residency. hard-evict reproduces too but leads to immediate 404 -> easier to detect.

maya: potential fixes I can think of: 1) cursor-residency indirection: cursor points to a logical prefix id + last-applied-version instead of physical residency id; 2) on rehydrate, atomically swap and invalidate cursors bound to old resid (plus a clear signal to streaming path to force refresh); 3) send a short TTLed tombstone on eviction that makes old entries return special marker for active cursors.

sam: preference towards minimal surface change. (2) seems doable: when we complete a rehydrate we publish an ordered eviction event: `{prefix, old_resid, new_resid, epoch}` and streaming path checks epoch before emitting tokens. cheap check.

maya: agree but race window: cursor in-flight between check and read might still access stale resid. we need either read-path to consult current mapping (small indirection) or make eviction sequenced so read-path if it sees old_resid also fetches mapping synchronously.

lee: implementation sketch: maintain in-memory prefix table: prefix -> {resid, epoch}. Reads accept resid param; if resid != table[prefix].resid then do one of: a) fail-fast with E_STALE so caller retries and gets updated map, b) block briefly and fetch new mapping (sync), c) attempt causal repair by merging streams (tricky). I'd pick (a) with a client-backoff & fast retry.

jonah: fwiw client retry is fine for internal streaming (we control SDK), but third-party integrators may not. Could we synthesize an internal short-lived redirect: response includes header `x-resid-mismatch: new_resid` so client can continue seamlessly?

sam: we already have per-token metadata plumbing for latency tracing. adding a mismatch header is small. server would return a special control-frame in stream: `RESID_REDIRECT new_resid epoch`. SDK treats as internal seek.

maya: tests: need a chaos test that interleaves soft-evict, rehydrate, and cursor writes across N=50k tokens. add property check: no token asserts older version than client-seen-vsn. also add smoke test that ensures redirect path does not duplicate tokens.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature flag `stream-resid-redirect` gated behind canary; add metric `stream.resid.mismatch_count` and `stream.resid.redirect_latency_ms`.

lee: one more tradeoff: sending redirects increases tail latency during churn. but it's better than silent correctness bugs. we should land as opt-in then roll to 100% after 2 weeks.

jonah: sounds good. i'll open a tiny RFC describing the control-frame + prefix table indirection + tests. will include simulation harness and perf impact numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:

maya: ping me on the RFC for review.

sam: will add SDK change to consume RESID_REDIRECT and seek safely.

jonah: attaching the minimal repro script later in thread.
